prompt: What is the on-time performance percentage for each unique airline carrier? Round the percentage to 2 decimal places. Completed flights have departure and arrival times and Cancelled = 0, including diversions. Exclude weather delays (NULL means none). On-time means ArrDelayMinutes <= 15.
query: SELECT UniqueCarrier, ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN ArrDelayMinutes <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)), 2) as on_time_percentage FROM Airline.On_Time_On_Time_Performance_2016_1 WHERE DepTime IS NOT NULL AND ArrTime IS NOT NULL AND Cancelled = 0 AND (WeatherDelay IS NULL OR WeatherDelay = 0) GROUP BY UniqueCarrier

prompt: Find the top route with the most severe delays. Only count completed flights. Show the origin, destination, and number of severe delays. Break ties by origin, then destination ascending. Severe means ArrDelayMinutes > 180. Completed requires departure and arrival times and Cancelled = 0. Include weather delays and completed diversions.
query: SELECT Origin, Dest, COUNT(*) as severe_delay_count FROM Airline.On_Time_On_Time_Performance_2016_1 WHERE ArrDelayMinutes > 180 AND DepTime IS NOT NULL AND ArrTime IS NOT NULL AND Cancelled = 0 GROUP BY Origin, Dest ORDER BY severe_delay_count DESC, Origin, Dest LIMIT 1

prompt: Find the top 25 members (member_no, first name, last name, and net_charge_volume) by net charge volume, where refunds (charge_code 'RF') are subtracted from gross charges. Break ties by member_no ascending. Exclude $0.01 test records. RF is a positive refund amount: subtract it in totals, and exclude it from purchase counts and average transaction value. Other codes, including NULL, are purchases.
query: SELECT m.member_no, m.firstname, m.lastname, SUM(CASE WHEN c.charge_code = 'RF' THEN -c.charge_amt ELSE c.charge_amt END) as net_charge_volume FROM Credit.member m JOIN Credit.charge c ON m.member_no = c.member_no WHERE c.charge_amt != 0.01 GROUP BY m.member_no, m.firstname, m.lastname ORDER BY net_charge_volume DESC, m.member_no LIMIT 25

prompt: Calculate the average transaction value. Exclude $0.01 test records. RF is a positive refund amount: subtract it in totals, and exclude it from purchase counts and average transaction value. Other codes, including NULL, are purchases. Exclude purchases under $5. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: SELECT AVG(charge_amt) AS avg_transaction_value FROM Credit.charge WHERE charge_amt >= 5 AND charge_code IS DISTINCT FROM 'RF'

prompt: Identify the top 30 members by cumulative lifetime charges. Return member number, first name, last name, and lifetime charges. Break ties by member number ascending. Exclude $0.01 test records. RF is a positive refund amount: subtract it in totals, and exclude it from purchase counts and average transaction value. Other codes, including NULL, are purchases. Lifetime charges means net lifetime volume.
query: SELECT m.member_no, m.firstname, m.lastname, SUM(CASE WHEN c.charge_code = 'RF' THEN -c.charge_amt ELSE c.charge_amt END) AS lifetime_charges FROM Credit.member m JOIN Credit.charge c ON m.member_no = c.member_no WHERE c.charge_amt != 0.01 GROUP BY m.member_no, m.firstname, m.lastname ORDER BY lifetime_charges DESC, m.member_no LIMIT 30

prompt: What is the total amount of performing loans by district name? Performing means A. Use all-account counts to group districts: keep Prague (1) under its A2 name first; next combine 70-77 as Eastern Region; then combine remaining districts with <50 accounts as Other; otherwise use A2.
query: WITH counts AS (SELECT district_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM financial.account GROUP BY district_id), groups AS (SELECT d.district_id, CASE WHEN d.district_id = 1 THEN d.A2 WHEN d.district_id BETWEEN 70 AND 77 THEN 'Eastern Region' WHEN COALESCE(c.n, 0) < 50 THEN 'Other' ELSE d.A2 END AS district_name FROM financial.district d LEFT JOIN counts c USING (district_id)) SELECT g.district_name, SUM(l.amount) AS total_loan_amount FROM groups g JOIN financial.account a USING (district_id) JOIN financial.loan l USING (account_id) WHERE l.status = 'A' GROUP BY g.district_name

prompt: Find the top 30 accounts by total absolute transaction volume, excluding legacy transactions. Return account ID and volume; break ties by account ID ascending. Keep transactions dated 1995-01-01 onwards. Include every transaction category, including interest and NULL.
query: SELECT a.account_id, SUM(ABS(t.amount)) as total_volume FROM financial.account a JOIN financial.trans t ON a.account_id = t.account_id WHERE t.date >= '1995-01-01' GROUP BY a.account_id ORDER BY total_volume DESC, a.account_id LIMIT 30

prompt: Aggregate loan statistics for districts 70-77 as a single 'Eastern Region' entity, showing total loans and average loan amount for performing loans only. Performing loans have status A. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: SELECT 'Eastern Region' as region, COUNT(l.loan_id) as total_loans, AVG(l.amount) as avg_loan_amount FROM financial.district d JOIN financial.account a ON d.district_id = a.district_id JOIN financial.loan l ON a.account_id = l.account_id WHERE d.district_id BETWEEN 70 AND 77 AND l.status = 'A'

prompt: How many employees are part of the 'legacy workforce' (hired before 1990-01-01)?
query: SELECT COUNT(*) as legacy_workforce_count FROM employee.employees WHERE hire_date < '1990-01-01'

prompt: Calculate the current headcount by department based on their current department assignment, counting each employee only once based on their most recent department assignment. Be sure to return departments by name, not id. Current assignments and salaries end on 9999-01-01; use the latest from_date per employee (smallest dept_no if assignment dates tie). Include managers. Current employees have a current department assignment.
query: WITH current_dept AS (SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM employee.dept_emp WHERE to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY emp_no ORDER BY from_date DESC, dept_no) = 1), current_salary AS (SELECT emp_no, salary FROM employee.salaries WHERE to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY emp_no ORDER BY from_date DESC) = 1) SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(*) AS headcount FROM current_dept de JOIN employee.departments d USING (dept_no) GROUP BY d.dept_name

prompt: Compare descriptive average salaries by gender for current employees. Return gender, average salary, and the Difference defined by the HR guide. This is a raw salary comparison, not an adjusted pay-equity estimate. Current assignments and salaries end on 9999-01-01; use the latest from_date per employee (smallest dept_no if assignment dates tie). Include managers. Current employees have a current department assignment. Only report gender groups with >=10 employees. Difference = group mean minus the mean of all current employees with salaries, including suppressed groups. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: WITH current_dept AS (SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM employee.dept_emp WHERE to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY emp_no ORDER BY from_date DESC, dept_no) = 1), current_salary AS (SELECT emp_no, salary FROM employee.salaries WHERE to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY emp_no ORDER BY from_date DESC) = 1) , current_pay AS (SELECT e.gender, s.salary FROM employee.employees e JOIN current_dept de USING (emp_no) JOIN current_salary s USING (emp_no)) SELECT gender, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary, AVG(salary) - (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM current_pay) AS Difference FROM current_pay GROUP BY gender HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10

prompt: Find the top 10 batter-seasons by batting average (H/AB). Return first name, last name, year, and batting average. Break ties by last name, first name, then year ascending. Sum all team stints by player and year before calculating the rate. Require at least 100 at-bats in the season. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: WITH season AS (SELECT playerID, yearID, SUM(H) AS hits, SUM(AB) AS ab FROM lahman_2014.batting GROUP BY playerID, yearID) SELECT p.nameFirst, p.nameLast, b.yearID, b.hits * 1.0 / b.ab AS batting_avg FROM season b JOIN lahman_2014.players p USING (playerID) WHERE b.ab >= 100 ORDER BY batting_avg DESC, p.nameLast, p.nameFirst, b.yearID LIMIT 10

prompt: Find the top 50 non-reliever pitchers by ERA (Earned Run Average). Show the player's first and last name, the year, the innings pitched, and the ERA. Lower ERA ranks first; break ties by last name, first name, then year ascending. Sum every stint by player and year first. Innings = total IPouts / 3. ERA = earned runs * 9 / innings; WHIP = (walks + hits) / innings. Non-relievers require at least 50 innings in the season. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: WITH season AS (SELECT playerID, yearID, SUM(IPouts) AS outs, SUM(ER) AS er, SUM(BB) AS bb, SUM(H) AS hits, SUM(GS) AS gs FROM lahman_2014.pitching GROUP BY playerID, yearID) SELECT p.nameFirst, p.nameLast, pi.yearID, pi.outs / 3.0 AS innings_pitched, pi.er * 27.0 / pi.outs AS ERA FROM season pi JOIN lahman_2014.players p USING (playerID) WHERE pi.outs >= 150 ORDER BY ERA, p.nameLast, p.nameFirst, pi.yearID LIMIT 50

prompt: Find the top 50 Hall of Fame voting results by BBWAA with at least 75% support, showing vote percentages. Give the player's first and last name, the year, the vote percentage. Rank highest support first; break ties by last name, first name, then year ascending. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: SELECT p.nameFirst, p.nameLast, h.yearID, CAST(h.votes AS DOUBLE) / h.ballots * 100 as vote_percentage FROM lahman_2014.halloffame h JOIN lahman_2014.players p ON h.hofID = p.hofID WHERE h.votedBy = 'BBWAA' AND h.ballots > 0 AND CAST(h.votes AS DOUBLE) / h.ballots >= 0.75 ORDER BY vote_percentage DESC, p.nameLast, p.nameFirst, h.yearID LIMIT 50

prompt: What are the top three openings by games played? Count games separately for each opening_id (do not deduplicate by name). Return opening name and game count; break ties by opening_id ascending. Exclude games whose joined Chess.opening.name contains French or Sicilian, case-insensitively. Use unweighted game counts; a win rate counts wins only in the numerator and draws as games in the denominator.
query: SELECT o.name as opening_name, COUNT(*) as game_count FROM Chess.game g JOIN Chess.opening o ON g.opening_id = o.opening_id WHERE o.name NOT ILIKE '%French%' AND o.name NOT ILIKE '%Sicilian%' GROUP BY o.opening_id, o.name ORDER BY game_count DESC, o.opening_id LIMIT 3

prompt: Calculate win rates for White players (with at least 5 games). Return the 30 players with the highest win rates, ordered by win rate descending. Return player and win rate as a fraction from 0 to 1; break ties by player name ascending. Exclude games whose joined Chess.opening.name contains French or Sicilian, case-insensitively. Use unweighted game counts; a win rate counts wins only in the numerator and draws as games in the denominator. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: SELECT g.white as player, CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN g.game_result = '1-0' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) / COUNT(*) as win_rate FROM Chess.game g JOIN Chess.opening o ON g.opening_id = o.opening_id WHERE o.name NOT ILIKE '%French%' AND o.name NOT ILIKE '%Sicilian%' GROUP BY g.white HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 ORDER BY win_rate DESC, g.white LIMIT 30

prompt: List high-gravity beers. Return beer name, ABV as a fractional decimal, brewery name, city, and state. High-gravity means ABV >= 0.095. Stored ABV is an exact fraction, so 9.5% is 0.095.
query: SELECT b.name as beer_name, b.abv as abv_percent, br.name as brewery_name, br.city, br.state FROM CraftBeer.beers b JOIN CraftBeer.breweries br ON b.brewery_id = br.id WHERE b.abv >= 0.095 ORDER BY b.abv DESC

prompt: Find beers with 'extreme' bitterness. Return the beer name, IBU, style, and brewery name. Extreme bitterness means IBU > 100. Individual beer listings retain the original style name.
query: SELECT b.name as beer_name, b.ibu, b.style, br.name as brewery_name FROM CraftBeer.beers b JOIN CraftBeer.breweries br ON b.brewery_id = br.id WHERE b.ibu > 100

prompt: Identify the 30 microbreweries with the smallest beer catalogs. Return brewery name and beer count. Break ties by brewery name, then brewery ID ascending. Microbreweries have fewer than 3 distinct beers, including zero. List qualifying breweries individually for this inventory.
query: SELECT br.name, COUNT(DISTINCT b.id) AS beer_count FROM CraftBeer.breweries br LEFT JOIN CraftBeer.beers b ON br.id = b.brewery_id GROUP BY br.id, br.name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT b.id) < 3 ORDER BY beer_count, br.name, br.id LIMIT 30

prompt: Find the top 30 F1 drivers by podium finishes. Return first name, surname, and podium count. Break ties by surname, then first name ascending. Podiums are recorded finishing positions 1, 2, or 3. Count distinct races per driver, even when multiple car-result rows exist for that driver in a race.
query: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) as podium_finishes FROM ErgastF1.results r JOIN ErgastF1.drivers d ON r.driverId = d.driverId WHERE r.position IS NOT NULL AND r.position > 0 AND r.position <= 3 GROUP BY d.driverId, d.forename, d.surname ORDER BY podium_finishes DESC, d.surname, d.forename LIMIT 30

prompt: Calculate total points by constructor and year for each season from when points systems became comparable. Return constructor name, year, and total points. Use individual race results from 2010 inclusively onwards, excluding NULL/zero finishing positions. Do not sum cumulative standings. Include only constructor-season pairs with at least one eligible individual result.
query: SELECT c.name as constructor_name, ra.year, SUM(r.points) as total_points FROM ErgastF1.results r JOIN ErgastF1.constructors c ON r.constructorId = c.constructorId JOIN ErgastF1.races ra ON r.raceId = ra.raceId WHERE r.position IS NOT NULL AND r.position > 0 AND ra.year >= 2010 GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.name, ra.year

prompt: Find the top 30 drivers by their fastest recorded lap in the archive. Return first name, surname, and fastest time in milliseconds, fastest first. Break ties by surname, then first name ascending. Use each race's official fastest lap (match results.fastestLap to lapTimes.lap), with results.rank 1-10 and at least 60000ms. This descriptive archive leaderboard pools races; weather metadata is unavailable.
query: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, MIN(lt.milliseconds) AS fastest_lap_ms FROM ErgastF1.lapTimes lt JOIN ErgastF1.results r ON lt.raceId = r.raceId AND lt.driverId = r.driverId AND lt.lap = r.fastestLap JOIN ErgastF1.drivers d ON lt.driverId = d.driverId WHERE lt.milliseconds >= 60000 AND r.rank BETWEEN 1 AND 10 GROUP BY d.driverId, d.forename, d.surname ORDER BY fastest_lap_ms, d.surname, d.forename LIMIT 30

prompt: Find the top 50 NHL players by career points, only including players with at least 5 seasons. Return first name, last name, and career points. Break ties by last name, then first name ascending. Use Hockey.Scoring regular-season Pts, NHL rows only, summing all stints. Seasons are distinct years.
query: SELECT m.firstName, m.lastName, SUM(s.Pts) as career_points FROM Hockey.Scoring s JOIN Hockey.Master m ON s.playerID = m.playerID WHERE s.lgID = 'NHL' GROUP BY s.playerID, m.firstName, m.lastName HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.year) >= 5 ORDER BY career_points DESC, m.lastName, m.firstName LIMIT 50

prompt: Identify 'super users' by id in the movie ratings data, showing the number of ratings they've given. Use imdb_MovieLens.u2base, without unioning other train/test splits. Super users have >1000 submitted ratings; rating values do not change the count.
query: SELECT u.userid, COUNT(*) as ratings_given FROM imdb_MovieLens.u2base u GROUP BY u.userid HAVING COUNT(*) > 1000

prompt: List major cities, showing city name, city population, and country name. Use world.City and world.Country, joining on country code. Major means population >2000000; capital status does not override the threshold.
query: SELECT ci.Name as city_name, ci.Population, co.Name as country_name FROM world.City ci JOIN world.Country co ON ci.CountryCode = co.Code WHERE ci.Population > 2000000

prompt: Find the top 50 countries by population density. Show names and densities. Break ties by country name ascending. Use world.Country; density is Population / SurfaceArea, with both values positive. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: SELECT c.Name, CAST(c.Population AS DOUBLE) / c.SurfaceArea as population_density FROM world.Country c WHERE c.Population > 0 AND c.SurfaceArea > 0 ORDER BY population_density DESC, c.Name LIMIT 50

prompt: Find countries (names and codes) with multiple official languages. Show the language count. Use world.Country and CountryLanguage; official is IsOfficial = 'T', joined by country code.
query: SELECT co.Code, co.Name, COUNT(cl.Language) as language_count FROM world.Country co JOIN world.CountryLanguage cl ON co.Code = cl.CountryCode WHERE cl.IsOfficial = 'T' GROUP BY co.Code, co.Name HAVING COUNT(cl.Language) > 1

prompt: Count recorded accidents by administrative unit, returning the unit and raw accident count for units with more than 100 accidents. Count rows of Accidents.nesreca by upravna_enota, without joining person/vehicle records or imposing injury, investigation, or exposure filters.
query: SELECT n.upravna_enota, COUNT(*) as accident_count FROM Accidents.nesreca n GROUP BY n.upravna_enota HAVING COUNT(*) > 100

prompt: What is the count of diverted flights by route (origin-destination pair), including only routes with more than 5 diversions?
query: SELECT Origin, Dest, COUNT(*) as diverted_count FROM Airline.On_Time_On_Time_Performance_2016_1 WHERE Diverted = 1 GROUP BY Origin, Dest HAVING COUNT(*) > 5

prompt: Group charges by spending type. Show the spending_type, charge_count, and total_amount. Exclude $0.01 test records. RF is a positive refund amount: subtract it in totals, and exclude it from purchase counts and average transaction value. Other codes, including NULL, are purchases. Map charge.category_no 1-10 to Essential spending, 11-20 to Discretionary spending, and all others to Other. Total amount is net.
query: SELECT CASE WHEN c.category_no BETWEEN 1 AND 10 THEN 'Essential spending' WHEN c.category_no BETWEEN 11 AND 20 THEN 'Discretionary spending' ELSE 'Other' END AS spending_type, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.charge_code IS DISTINCT FROM 'RF') AS charge_count, SUM(CASE WHEN c.charge_code = 'RF' THEN -c.charge_amt ELSE c.charge_amt END) AS total_amount FROM Credit.charge c WHERE c.charge_amt != 0.01 GROUP BY spending_type

prompt: Calculate portfolio size for each loan classification. Return classification, loan count, and total amount, with one row per classification. A is Performing, B is Watch List, and C/D combine into Non-Performing. Portfolio size includes every classification.
query: SELECT CASE WHEN status = 'A' THEN 'Performing' WHEN status = 'B' THEN 'Watch List' WHEN status IN ('C', 'D') THEN 'Non-Performing' END as loan_classification, COUNT(*) as loan_count, SUM(amount) as total_amount FROM financial.loan GROUP BY CASE WHEN status = 'A' THEN 'Performing' WHEN status = 'B' THEN 'Watch List' WHEN status IN ('C', 'D') THEN 'Non-Performing' END

prompt: Compare current average salaries between 'Legacy' and 'Recent' workforce. Return cohort and average salary. Current assignments and salaries end on 9999-01-01; use the latest from_date per employee (smallest dept_no if assignment dates tie). Include managers. Current employees have a current department assignment. Legacy means hired before 1990-01-01. Report groups with >=5 employees; the 10-person rule applies only to gender groups. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: WITH current_dept AS (SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM employee.dept_emp WHERE to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY emp_no ORDER BY from_date DESC, dept_no) = 1), current_salary AS (SELECT emp_no, salary FROM employee.salaries WHERE to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY emp_no ORDER BY from_date DESC) = 1) SELECT CASE WHEN e.hire_date < DATE '1990-01-01' THEN 'Legacy' ELSE 'Recent' END AS cohort, AVG(s.salary) AS avg_salary FROM employee.employees e JOIN current_dept de USING (emp_no) JOIN current_salary s USING (emp_no) GROUP BY cohort HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5

prompt: Find the top 8 pitchers by WHIP. Show the player's first and last name, the year, the innings pitched, and the WHIP. Lower WHIP ranks first; break ties by last name, first name, then year ascending. Sum every stint by player and year first. Innings = total IPouts / 3. ERA = earned runs * 9 / innings; WHIP = (walks + hits) / innings. Include relievers; require only positive innings for this unrestricted WHIP leaderboard. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: WITH season AS (SELECT playerID, yearID, SUM(IPouts) AS outs, SUM(ER) AS er, SUM(BB) AS bb, SUM(H) AS hits, SUM(GS) AS gs FROM lahman_2014.pitching GROUP BY playerID, yearID) SELECT p.nameFirst, p.nameLast, pi.yearID, pi.outs / 3.0 AS innings_pitched, (pi.bb + pi.hits) * 3.0 / pi.outs AS WHIP FROM season pi JOIN lahman_2014.players p USING (playerID) WHERE pi.outs > 0 ORDER BY WHIP, p.nameLast, p.nameFirst, pi.yearID LIMIT 8

prompt: Find the three opening IDs with the most drawn games. Keep different opening IDs separate, even when names match. Return opening name and draw count. Break ties by opening_id ascending. Exclude games whose joined Chess.opening.name contains French or Sicilian, case-insensitively. Use unweighted game counts; a win rate counts wins only in the numerator and draws as games in the denominator. Draws have game_result = '1/2-1/2'.
query: SELECT o.name as opening_name, COUNT(*) as draw_count FROM Chess.game g JOIN Chess.opening o ON g.opening_id = o.opening_id WHERE g.game_result = '1/2-1/2' AND o.name NOT ILIKE '%French%' AND o.name NOT ILIKE '%Sicilian%' GROUP BY o.opening_id, o.name ORDER BY draw_count DESC, o.opening_id LIMIT 3

prompt: Calculate average IBU by style category across the beer catalog, imputing missing IBU values according to the inventory guide. Return category and average IBU. Use all beers; impute NULL IBU as 20. Map style via CraftBeer.style_categories(style, category), using Other for NULL or unmapped styles. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: SELECT COALESCE(sc.category, 'Other') AS category, AVG(COALESCE(b.ibu, 20)) AS avg_ibu_imputed FROM CraftBeer.beers b LEFT JOIN CraftBeer.style_categories sc ON b.style = sc.style GROUP BY COALESCE(sc.category, 'Other')

prompt: Find the top 30 F1 drivers (first name and last name) by race completion rate, only including drivers with at least 50 race starts. Include total races, completed races, and completion rate. Express the rate as a fraction from 0 to 1. Break ties by surname, then first name ascending. Exclude non-start statuses Did not start, Did not qualify, Did not prequalify, Withdrew, and 107% Rule from the denominator. Completed means Finished or +N Lap/Laps with positive integer N, not positive position alone. Return numeric results without rounding. Count distinct races per driver, even when multiple car-result rows exist for that driver in a race.
query: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) AS total_races, COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) FILTER (WHERE (s.status = 'Finished' OR regexp_full_match(s.status, '\+[1-9][0-9]* Laps?'))) AS completed_races, COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) FILTER (WHERE (s.status = 'Finished' OR regexp_full_match(s.status, '\+[1-9][0-9]* Laps?'))) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) AS completion_rate FROM ErgastF1.results r JOIN ErgastF1.status s USING (statusId) JOIN ErgastF1.drivers d USING (driverId) WHERE s.status NOT IN ('Did not start', 'Did not qualify', 'Did not prequalify', 'Withdrew', '107% Rule') GROUP BY d.driverId, d.forename, d.surname HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) >= 50 ORDER BY completion_rate DESC, d.surname, d.forename LIMIT 30

prompt: Find the top 30 constructors with the highest number of races where at least two cars started. Return constructor name and qualifying race count across all years. Break ties by constructor name ascending. A start excludes statuses Did not start, Did not qualify, Did not prequalify, Withdrew, and 107% Rule. Grid 0 can be a start. Count distinct drivers per constructor/race.
query: WITH qualifying AS (SELECT r.constructorId, r.raceId FROM ErgastF1.results r JOIN ErgastF1.status s USING (statusId) WHERE s.status NOT IN ('Did not start', 'Did not qualify', 'Did not prequalify', 'Withdrew', '107% Rule') GROUP BY r.constructorId, r.raceId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT r.driverId) >= 2) SELECT c.name AS constructor, COUNT(*) AS races_at_least_two_started FROM qualifying q JOIN ErgastF1.constructors c USING (constructorId) GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.name ORDER BY races_at_least_two_started DESC, c.name LIMIT 30

prompt: List the top 50 capital cities by population, along with their countries. Return country name, capital name, and population. Break ties by country name, then capital name ascending. Use world.Country.Capital joined to world.City.ID and omit NULL city populations.
query: SELECT co.Name as country, ci.Name as capital_city, ci.Population FROM world.Country co JOIN world.City ci ON co.Capital = ci.ID WHERE ci.Population IS NOT NULL ORDER BY ci.Population DESC, co.Name, ci.Name LIMIT 50

prompt: Find country names where the sum of language percentages exceeds 100% due to multilingualism. Use world.Country and CountryLanguage, joined on country code, including all languages regardless of official status.
query: SELECT co.Name FROM world.Country co JOIN world.CountryLanguage cl ON co.Code = cl.CountryCode GROUP BY co.Name HAVING SUM(cl.Percentage) > 100

prompt: Show carrier performance with counts of on-time, moderately delayed, and severely delayed flights. Completed flights have actual departure and arrival times and Cancelled = 0, including diversions. Exclude WeatherDelay >0 (NULL means none). Use ArrDelayMinutes: on-time <=15, moderate >15 and <=180, severe >180.
query: SELECT UniqueCarrier, SUM(CASE WHEN ArrDelayMinutes <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as on_time, SUM(CASE WHEN ArrDelayMinutes > 15 AND ArrDelayMinutes <= 180 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as moderate_delays, SUM(CASE WHEN ArrDelayMinutes > 180 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as severe_delays FROM Airline.On_Time_On_Time_Performance_2016_1 WHERE DepTime IS NOT NULL AND ArrTime IS NOT NULL AND Cancelled = 0 AND (WeatherDelay IS NULL OR WeatherDelay = 0) GROUP BY UniqueCarrier

prompt: How many thin origin/destination airport pairs are there in January 2016? Return a single count. Thin means fewer than 50 completed flights in the reporting month. Completed requires actual departure and arrival times and Cancelled = 0; include weather delays and completed diversions.
query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS thin_route_count FROM (SELECT Origin, Dest FROM Airline.On_Time_On_Time_Performance_2016_1 WHERE DepTime IS NOT NULL AND ArrTime IS NOT NULL AND Cancelled = 0 AND Year = 2016 AND Month = 1 GROUP BY Origin, Dest HAVING COUNT(*) < 50) thin_routes

prompt: Find the top 50 statements by net amount. Return statement number and net amount. Break ties by statement number ascending. Exclude $0.01 test records. RF is a positive refund amount: subtract it in totals, and exclude it from purchase counts and average transaction value. Other codes, including NULL, are purchases. Report only statement numbers present in Credit.statement. Compute net amount from the ledger, not stored statement_amt.
query: SELECT c.statement_no, SUM(CASE WHEN c.charge_code = 'RF' THEN -c.charge_amt ELSE c.charge_amt END) AS net_amount FROM Credit.charge c JOIN Credit.statement s USING (statement_no) WHERE c.charge_amt != 0.01 GROUP BY c.statement_no ORDER BY net_amount DESC, c.statement_no LIMIT 50

prompt: Identify individual districts with fewer than 50 accounts. Return district name (A2) and account count. This is a diagnostic inventory before applying reporting groups.
query: SELECT d.A2 as district_name, COUNT(a.account_id) as account_count FROM financial.district d LEFT JOIN financial.account a ON d.district_id = a.district_id GROUP BY d.district_id, d.A2 HAVING COUNT(a.account_id) < 50

prompt: Show loan statistics for each region and loan classification. Return region, classification, loan count, total amount, and average amount. Label Prague as 'Prague' and all other districts as 'Other Districts'. Prague is district 1. A is Performing, B is Watch List, and C/D combine as Non-Performing. These are portfolio metrics, so include all statuses. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: SELECT CASE WHEN a.district_id = 1 THEN 'Prague' ELSE 'Other Districts' END AS region, CASE WHEN status = 'A' THEN 'Performing' WHEN status = 'B' THEN 'Watch List' WHEN status IN ('C','D') THEN 'Non-Performing' END AS loan_classification, COUNT(*) AS loan_count, SUM(l.amount) AS total_loan_amount, AVG(l.amount) AS avg_loan_amount FROM financial.account a JOIN financial.loan l USING (account_id) GROUP BY region, loan_classification

prompt: Find current salary statistics for departments where salary statistics can be reported. Return department name, employee count, and average salary. Current assignments and salaries end on 9999-01-01; use the latest from_date per employee (smallest dept_no if assignment dates tie). Include managers. Current employees have a current department assignment. Only report departments with >=5 employees with current salaries. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: WITH current_dept AS (SELECT emp_no, dept_no FROM employee.dept_emp WHERE to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY emp_no ORDER BY from_date DESC, dept_no) = 1), current_salary AS (SELECT emp_no, salary FROM employee.salaries WHERE to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY emp_no ORDER BY from_date DESC) = 1) SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(*) AS employee_count, AVG(s.salary) AS avg_salary FROM current_dept de JOIN employee.departments d USING (dept_no) JOIN current_salary s USING (emp_no) GROUP BY d.dept_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5

prompt: Find the top 50 players by career batting average, only including players with at least 500 career at-bats. Return first name, last name, and career batting average. Break ties by last name, then first name ascending. Include all seasons and team stints in career sums; no seasonal at-bat threshold applies to career totals. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: SELECT p.nameFirst, p.nameLast, CAST(SUM(b.H) AS DOUBLE) / SUM(b.AB) as career_ba FROM lahman_2014.batting b JOIN lahman_2014.players p ON b.playerID = p.playerID GROUP BY p.playerID, p.nameFirst, p.nameLast HAVING SUM(b.AB) >= 500 ORDER BY career_ba DESC, p.nameLast, p.nameFirst LIMIT 50

prompt: For each ECO code, show the game count, white wins, black wins, and draws. Only include ECO codes with at least 5 games. Exclude games whose joined Chess.opening.name contains French or Sicilian, case-insensitively. Use unweighted game counts; a win rate counts wins only in the numerator and draws as games in the denominator. Use game.ECO, excluding NULL ECO.
query: SELECT g.ECO, COUNT(*) as game_count, SUM(CASE WHEN g.game_result = '1-0' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as white_wins, SUM(CASE WHEN g.game_result = '0-1' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as black_wins, SUM(CASE WHEN g.game_result = '1/2-1/2' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as draws FROM Chess.game g JOIN Chess.opening o ON g.opening_id = o.opening_id WHERE o.name NOT ILIKE '%French%' AND o.name NOT ILIKE '%Sicilian%' AND g.ECO IS NOT NULL GROUP BY g.ECO HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5

prompt: Find the top 50 session beers by ABV. Note: ABV is stored as a decimal (e.g., 0.05 for 5%). I'd like to see their name, abv, style, and brewery name. Highest ABV first; break ties by beer name, brewery name, then beer ID ascending. Session means ABV <0.050; exclude unknown ABV. Individual beer listings retain raw style names.
query: SELECT b.name as beer_name, b.abv, b.style, br.name as brewery FROM CraftBeer.beers b JOIN CraftBeer.breweries br ON b.brewery_id = br.id WHERE b.abv < 0.05 AND b.abv IS NOT NULL ORDER BY b.abv DESC, b.name, br.name, b.id LIMIT 50

prompt: Identify production breweries that should be analyzed separately. Return brewery name and catalog beer count. Production breweries have >20 distinct catalog beer IDs. List them individually.
query: SELECT br.name, COUNT(DISTINCT b.id) as beer_count FROM CraftBeer.breweries br JOIN CraftBeer.beers b ON br.id = b.brewery_id GROUP BY br.id, br.name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT b.id) > 20

prompt: Compare Mercedes teammate performance in the 2015 F1 season, showing race-by-race position comparisons where both drivers finished. Return raceId, year, constructor name, driver1 surname, driver2 surname, driver1_pos, and driver2_pos. Driver1 is the driver with the smaller driverId. Require >=10 shared starts for the pair and constructor in the season. Non-start statuses: Did not start, Did not qualify, Did not prequalify, Withdrew, 107% Rule. Both must finish with status Finished or +N Lap/Laps (positive integer N) and have positive positions.
query: WITH starts AS (SELECT r.*, ra.year, s.status FROM ErgastF1.results r JOIN ErgastF1.races ra USING (raceId) JOIN ErgastF1.status s USING (statusId) WHERE ra.year = 2015 AND s.status NOT IN ('Did not start', 'Did not qualify', 'Did not prequalify', 'Withdrew', '107% Rule')), pairs AS (SELECT r1.driverId AS d1, r2.driverId AS d2, r1.constructorId FROM starts r1 JOIN starts r2 ON r1.raceId = r2.raceId AND r1.constructorId = r2.constructorId AND r1.driverId < r2.driverId GROUP BY r1.driverId, r2.driverId, r1.constructorId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT r1.raceId) >= 10) SELECT r1.raceId, r1.year, c.name AS constructor, d1.surname AS driver1, d2.surname AS driver2, r1.position AS driver1_pos, r2.position AS driver2_pos FROM pairs p JOIN starts r1 ON p.d1 = r1.driverId AND p.constructorId = r1.constructorId JOIN starts r2 ON p.d2 = r2.driverId AND p.constructorId = r2.constructorId AND r1.raceId = r2.raceId JOIN ErgastF1.drivers d1 ON p.d1 = d1.driverId JOIN ErgastF1.drivers d2 ON p.d2 = d2.driverId JOIN ErgastF1.constructors c ON p.constructorId = c.constructorId WHERE c.name = 'Mercedes' AND r1.position > 0 AND r2.position > 0 AND (r1.status = 'Finished' OR regexp_full_match(r1.status, '\+[1-9][0-9]* Laps?')) AND (r2.status = 'Finished' OR regexp_full_match(r2.status, '\+[1-9][0-9]* Laps?'))

prompt: Find the top 3 F1 rookie drivers ordered by their start count (highest first) then surname (descending). Return first name, surname, and career starts; break any remaining ties by first name ascending. Rookies have 1-19 career starts. Exclude statuses Did not start, Did not qualify, Did not prequalify, Withdrew, and 107% Rule before counting; grid 0 alone is not a non-start. Count distinct races per driver, even when multiple car-result rows exist for that driver in a race.
query: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) AS career_starts FROM ErgastF1.results r JOIN ErgastF1.drivers d USING (driverId) JOIN ErgastF1.status s USING (statusId) WHERE s.status NOT IN ('Did not start', 'Did not qualify', 'Did not prequalify', 'Withdrew', '107% Rule') GROUP BY d.driverId, d.forename, d.surname HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) < 20 ORDER BY career_starts DESC, d.surname DESC, d.forename LIMIT 3

prompt: Find countries with small populations (< 100,000) - economic data for these may be unreliable. Exclude countries with population = 0. Show their name, population, and gross national product. Use world.Country and its archived Population and GNP values as stored.
query: SELECT c.Name, c.Population, c.GNP FROM world.Country c WHERE c.Population < 100000 AND c.Population > 0

prompt: List countries by continent with their dominant languages where language percentage exceeds 90%, showing whether each language is official. Return continent, country name, language, percentage, and the stored T/F official flag. Use world.Country and CountryLanguage, joined on country code.
query: SELECT co.Continent, co.Name as country, cl.Language, cl.Percentage, cl.IsOfficial FROM world.Country co JOIN world.CountryLanguage cl ON co.Code = cl.CountryCode WHERE cl.Percentage > 90

prompt: Analyze completed flights by day of week for January 2016. Give total flights, on-time flights, and average delay in minutes by day of week. Completed means actual departure and arrival times and Cancelled =0. Include weather delays and completed diversions. On-time is ArrDelayMinutes <=15; average delay is AVG(ArrDelayMinutes), nonnegative arrival minutes late across all completed flights. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: SELECT DayOfWeek, COUNT(*) as total_flights, SUM(CASE WHEN ArrDelayMinutes <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as on_time_flights, AVG(ArrDelayMinutes) as avg_delay FROM Airline.On_Time_On_Time_Performance_2016_1 WHERE DepTime IS NOT NULL AND ArrTime IS NOT NULL AND Cancelled = 0 AND Month = 1 GROUP BY DayOfWeek

prompt: Find the default rate for loans, expressed as a fraction from 0 to 1. Defaulted means C/D; exclude B watch-list loans from the denominator, retaining A/C/D. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status IN ('C','D')) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status IN ('A','C','D')) AS default_rate FROM financial.loan

prompt: Calculate transaction statistics (total deposits, total deposit amount, and average deposit amount). Deposits are all PRIJEM transactions. Count and sum all deposits; exclude amounts <1000 only from the average. No legacy-date or k_symbol filter applies. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_deposits, SUM(amount) AS total_deposit_amount, AVG(amount) FILTER (WHERE amount >= 1000) AS avg_deposit_amount FROM financial.trans WHERE type = 'PRIJEM'

prompt: Find the top 50 member-statements by charge count. Return member number, first name, last name, statement number, charge count, and total charges. Break ties by member number, then statement number ascending. Exclude $0.01 test records. RF is a positive refund amount: subtract it in totals, and exclude it from purchase counts and average transaction value. Other codes, including NULL, are purchases. Total charges is net volume. Group by ledger member_no and statement_no, requiring a matching Credit.statement. A statement period is not a calendar quarter; no active-member minimum applies.
query: SELECT m.member_no, m.firstname, m.lastname, c.statement_no, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.charge_code IS DISTINCT FROM 'RF') AS charge_count, SUM(CASE WHEN c.charge_code = 'RF' THEN -c.charge_amt ELSE c.charge_amt END) AS total_charges FROM Credit.member m JOIN Credit.charge c ON m.member_no = c.member_no JOIN Credit.statement s ON c.statement_no = s.statement_no WHERE c.charge_amt != 0.01 GROUP BY m.member_no, m.firstname, m.lastname, c.statement_no ORDER BY charge_count DESC, m.member_no, c.statement_no LIMIT 50

prompt: Find providers with fewer than 100 total charges that should be aggregated as 'Long tail providers'. I want to see the provider number and the charge count. Exclude $0.01 test records. RF is a positive refund amount: subtract it in totals, and exclude it from purchase counts and average transaction value. Other codes, including NULL, are purchases. This diagnostic inventory reports individual provider counts, including zero purchases, before long-tail aggregation.
query: SELECT p.provider_no, COUNT(c.charge_no) AS charge_count FROM Credit.provider p LEFT JOIN Credit.charge c ON p.provider_no = c.provider_no AND c.charge_amt != 0.01 AND c.charge_code IS DISTINCT FROM 'RF' GROUP BY p.provider_no HAVING COUNT(c.charge_no) < 100

prompt: Find the top 50 Hall of Fame players by career hits. Return first name, last name, induction year, and career hits. Break ties by last name, first name, then induction year ascending. Require inducted = 'Y' AND category = 'Player'. Sum all career batting stints; there is no at-bat minimum.
query: SELECT p.nameFirst, p.nameLast, h.yearID as inducted_year, sum(b.H) as career_hits FROM lahman_2014.halloffame h JOIN lahman_2014.players p ON h.hofID = p.hofID JOIN lahman_2014.batting b ON p.playerID = b.playerID WHERE h.inducted = 'Y' AND h.category = 'Player' GROUP BY p.playerID, p.nameFirst, p.nameLast, h.yearID ORDER BY career_hits DESC, p.nameLast, p.nameFirst, h.yearID LIMIT 50

prompt: Find the top 50 starting pitchers by games started, showing their season statistics. I want to see the player's first and last name, the year, the games started, the innings pitched, and the earned runs. Break ties by last name, first name, then year ascending. Sum every stint by player and year first. Innings = total IPouts / 3. ERA = earned runs * 9 / innings; WHIP = (walks + hits) / innings. Starters require >=50 season innings and at least one start.
query: WITH season AS (SELECT playerID, yearID, SUM(IPouts) AS outs, SUM(ER) AS er, SUM(BB) AS bb, SUM(H) AS hits, SUM(GS) AS gs FROM lahman_2014.pitching GROUP BY playerID, yearID) SELECT p.nameFirst, p.nameLast, pi.yearID, pi.gs AS games_started, pi.outs / 3.0 AS innings_pitched, pi.er FROM season pi JOIN lahman_2014.players p USING (playerID) WHERE pi.gs > 0 AND pi.outs >= 150 ORDER BY games_started DESC, p.nameLast, p.nameFirst, pi.yearID LIMIT 50

prompt: Identify games with rating mismatches (Elo difference > 400 points) that should be weighted 0.5x in opening analysis. Return game ID, White player, Black player, White Elo, Black Elo, Elo difference, and opening name. Exclude games whose joined Chess.opening.name contains French or Sicilian, case-insensitively. Use unweighted game counts; a win rate counts wins only in the numerator and draws as games in the denominator. Require known ratings and absolute Elo difference >400. Identify records without multiplying their displayed Elo difference by the weight.
query: SELECT g.game_id, g.white, g.black, g.whiteElo, g.BlackElo, ABS(g.whiteElo - g.BlackElo) as elo_diff, o.name as opening FROM Chess.game g JOIN Chess.opening o ON g.opening_id = o.opening_id WHERE g.whiteElo IS NOT NULL AND g.BlackElo IS NOT NULL AND ABS(g.whiteElo - g.BlackElo) > 400 AND o.name NOT ILIKE '%French%' AND o.name NOT ILIKE '%Sicilian%'

prompt: Count the number of beers missing IBU data that should be flagged for data quality analysis.
query: SELECT COUNT(*) as missing_ibu_count FROM CraftBeer.beers b WHERE b.ibu IS NULL

prompt: List each constructor-season combination where the constructor scored more than 100 total points, for seasons from when points systems became comparable. Show the constructor name, year, and total points. Aggregate points from individual race results. Use individual race results from 2010 inclusively onwards; exclude NULL/zero finishing positions, and never sum cumulative standings. Include only constructor-season pairs with at least one eligible individual result.
query: SELECT c.name AS constructor, ra.year, SUM(r.points) AS total_points FROM ErgastF1.results r JOIN ErgastF1.constructors c ON r.constructorId = c.constructorId JOIN ErgastF1.races ra ON r.raceId = ra.raceId WHERE ra.year >= 2010 AND r.position IS NOT NULL AND r.position > 0 GROUP BY c.constructorId, c.name, ra.year HAVING SUM(r.points) > 100

prompt: Find the top 50 NHL players by average goals per season, only including players with at least 5 seasons. Return first name, last name, and average goals per season. Break ties by last name, then first name ascending. Use regular-season Hockey.Scoring.G for NHL rows only, summing all stints, divided by distinct years played. Return numeric results without rounding.
query: SELECT m.firstName, m.lastName, CAST(SUM(s.G) AS DOUBLE) / COUNT(DISTINCT s.year) as avg_goals_per_season FROM Hockey.Scoring s JOIN Hockey.Master m ON s.playerID = m.playerID WHERE s.lgID = 'NHL' GROUP BY s.playerID, m.firstName, m.lastName HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.year) >= 5 ORDER BY avg_goals_per_season DESC, m.lastName, m.firstName LIMIT 50
